newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco imposes $34 tonne tax on soft wheat import.
newsitem.headline: Morocco imposes $34 tonne tax on soft wheat import.

text.p: Moroccan traders on Wednesday said the government has imposed new customs duties on soft wheat imports, equivalent to $34 per tonne.
"Following a previous government decision, the authorities imposed 31.20 dirhams ($3.4) per quintal (100 kg) of imported soft wheat," a Casablanca-based trader told Reuters.
The new tax took effect on January 25, 1997 and will remain in place until further notice, he added.
A cabinet meeting headed by Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali approved a week earlier a law raising customs duties on imported soft wheat, an official at the trade ministry said.
The increase was due to the importance of the domestic stock of wheat and relative fall in wheat prices on the international market, he said.
Morocco plans to import 1.0 million tonnes of soft wheat in the 1996/97 season, starting last July, the agriculture ministry has said.

The government move aimed to "protect small farmers and local industry because competition is becoming very tough," a member of the wheat importers association said. "The new customs duty will affect future soft wheat imports," he added but did not elaborate.
Morocco harvested 10 million tonnes of cereals, including 3.65 million tonnes of soft wheat in the 1995/96 season, the Statistics Directorate said recently.
Morocco in May 1996 launched a policy of gradual liberalisation for commodities trade over a four-year period to comply with agreements signed earlier with the WTO.

The country which has had cyclical periods of drought and good rains since 1990, plans also to safeguard what the authorities describe as a "strategic stock of wheat" estimated at between 2.5 and 3.0 million tonnes.
In 1995, Morocco suffered a catastrophic drought and had to import more than 2.5 million tonnes of cereals, including wheat.
